context_requirements: Homologous recombination deficiency (e.g., BRCA1/2 mutation, ATM loss, or HRD genomic scar) for strong single-agent sensitivity
SLFN11 expression for robust PARP inhibitor response in SCLC and other lines
Active DNA replication and proliferation to generate PARP-trapping lesions
Functional p53 pathway for transcriptional DNA damage response; TP53-mutant lines may show attenuated p21 induction
falsifiers: No induction of CDKN1A or other p53 target genes at 6 or 24 h in any line
No reduction in proliferation or G2/M genes at 24 h in any line
Strong and consistent transcriptional response in all nine lines, including non-proliferating or HR-proficient lines, contradicting the requirement for HR deficiency or replication
Absence of any DNA damage response signature (e.g., no GADD45A, MDM2, or TIPARP changes) at 24 h

evidence.supports: PARP inhibitor resistance is associated with increased ATR-CHK1 activity and replication fork stalling, suggesting DNA damage response and replication stress as downstream transcriptional consequences.
SLFN11 expression correlates with PARP inhibitor response in small cell lung cancer, indicating context-dependent sensitivity.
Synthetic lethal siRNA screen identifies CDK5 and other kinases mediating sensitivity to PARP inhibition, implicating cell-cycle checkpoint and DNA repair pathways.
CDK12 inhibition reverses PARP inhibitor resistance by disrupting homologous recombination, supporting HR status as a key determinant of response.
ATM-deficient lymphoid tumor cells are selectively killed by olaparib, demonstrating that loss of ATM-mediated DNA damage signaling confers PARP inhibitor sensitivity.
